title: Tryouts and Scholarship
premise: Orsen Sandoval transfers to Hollowmere Academy, a school whose founding families built it atop a sealed spring that grants the town prosperity — as long as the school 'gives back' a student every generation through the Tryouts, a brutal scholarship competition that secretly selects a sacrifice. When her new best friend Priya vanishes mid-competition, leaving behind a ring of keys that open doors no student should enter, Orsen discovers the scholarship is a lie and the town's wealth is bought with memory: each sacrifice is erased from every mind that loved them. To save Priya and end the tradition, Orsen must convince the founders' heirs to give up their power, and in the final chapter she chooses to carry the memories herself, surviving at the price of remembering what everyone else was allowed to forget.
about_author: Wendell Blackwood is a former boarding school teacher who spent a decade collecting the strange rituals and half-true legends of elite academies before turning them into fiction. He writes in an old converted gymnasium in upstate New York and swears the building hums at night.

chapters.title: The New Kid's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Arriving at Hollowmere Academy on a scholarship, she catalogs the school's odd rules — no one walks the east corridor alone, the bell rings thirteen times on Fridays — and meets sharp-tongued Priya Raval, who shows her the keys she's 'collecting.' Beat: cautious belonging, with dread underneath.

chapters.title: Tryouts Season
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The annual Tryouts begin: physical trials, puzzle rooms, and interviews that feel more like interrogations. Orsen excels despite herself, while Priya grows strangely intense, insisting Orsen sign up too. A teacher watches Orsen a beat too long. Beat: ambition curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Thirteen Rings
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. On the night the bell rings thirteen times, Priya disappears. Her dorm room is untouched; her family, contacted by phone, cheerfully insists they have no daughter. Only a heavy ring of keys remains, tucked in Orsen's bag. Beat: gaslit grief and the first hard proof.

chapters.title: Doors That Aren't Doors
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, with a brief Priya journal interlude. The keys open maintenance doors, a sub-basement, and finally a room of archived uniforms — one bearing Priya's name, dated forty years ago. Orsen realizes the Tryouts have run far longer than anyone admits. Beat: horror of scale.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. With reluctant ally Marcus — a Tryouts favorite and founder's grandson — she finds the Ledger: names, dates, and payments. The town's prosperity is contractual. Every winner of the scholarship 'earns' their future by becoming the spring's keeper below. Beat: power's machinery laid bare.

chapters.title: What the Spring Keeps
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Descending with the keys, she hears Priya's voice through the water and glimpses the previous keepers — preserved, aware, remembering everything while the town forgets them. She flees as the spring notices her. Beat: terror, and the theme of memory made literal.

chapters.title: Heirs and Apologies
chapters.summary: Alternating Orsen and Marcus POV. Marcus confronts his family; Orsen rallies students whose siblings and friends were 'transferred away.' The founders offer Orsen a deal: win the Tryouts, take Priya's place, and everyone stays comfortable. Beat: the corruption of power extends its hand.

chapters.title: Final Round
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. She enters the Tryouts' last trial intending to lose, but the school rigs it so she wins — the spring wants a keeper who remembers. In the winner's ceremony she's led toward the east corridor as the town applauds. Beat: triumph inverted into trap; cliff-edge tension.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Orsen and Marcus POV, converging underground. Marcus breaks the founders' seal from the archive side while Orsen refuses the spring's offer, offering it her memories of Priya instead — a bargain it cannot resist. The keepers are released; Priya surfaces, alive but hollowed. Beat: sacrifice that isn't death, but cost.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, months later. The school closes its east corridor; the town's fortunes wobble but hold. Priya rebuilds herself from Orsen's careful retellings, and the town slowly remembers its missing. Orsen keeps one key on a chain — the one that opens nothing now. Beat: survival, grief, and chosen memory.
